descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1953
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1933 to 1953 and has held a majority in Congress since the 1954 elections

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1953
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1933 to 1953 and has held a majority in Congress since the 1954 elections

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a States' Rights and a Socialist Labor nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Eisenhower, Nixon, Stevenson, Kefauver, Truman, Franklin Roosevelt, Andrews or Jones

slice_sources.men: 1950 and 1960 censuses interpolated to November 1956; men 21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky) outside the eleven Southern states, in the 48 states (no presidential vote in DC; Alaska and Hawaii were territories); calibrated to certified 1956 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1950 and 1960 censuses interpolated to November 1956; women 21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky) outside the eleven Southern states, in the 48 states (no presidential vote in DC; Alaska and Hawaii were territories); calibrated to certified 1956 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 1950 and 1960 censuses interpolated to November 1956; white adults (21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky)) in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults), where poll taxes still applied in Alabama, Arkansas, Mississippi, Texas and Virginia; calibrated to certified 1956 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1950 and 1960 censuses interpolated to November 1956; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; registration held to roughly a quarter of Black adults by literacy tests, poll taxes, registrar discretion and intimidation. The shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1950 and 1960 censuses interpolated to November 1956; foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized citizens (aliens could not vote in any state).

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
